title: EU-exclusive traffic holdout and tenant safelisting
creator: Aisha Khan
body: Problem: Several enterprise customers require a strict EU-only enforcement mode during onboarding and during regulatory audits. Current residency checks are advisory and sometimes allow fallthrough to non-EU variants when capacity is constrained. We need a deterministic, testable enforcement layer that supports tenant safelisting (allowlist) and tenant denylisting, plus a temporary holdout mode that prevents any outbound egress outside EU regions unless explicitly safelisted.\n\nGoal: Implement an "EU-exclusive holdout" routing policy that can be toggled per-tenant, plus a tenant safelist/denylist management surface for the policy engine. The implementation must: (1) enforce routing to EU-only model endpoints for flagged tenants; (2) support soft-safelist (alert + audit but still block) and hard-safelist modes; (3) expose audit logs and reason codes for each decision; (4) be compatible with Dedicated and Private modes; (5) provide clear operator controls for emergency overrides and observable metrics for compliance audits.
acceptance_criteria: Policy expression: new 'eu_exclusive' predicate added to routing policy language and evaluated in the PDP (policy decision point)
Tenant metadata: tenants can have 'eu_holdout' = {off|soft|hard} and 'safelist_reasons' stored in tenant profile
Routing behavior: for hard holdout, requests for tenants with eu_holdout=hard must never route to non-EU endpoints; for soft holdout, route must be blocked but an automated ticket + alert is created
Allow/Deny surface: Console and API endpoints for adding/removing tenants from safelist/denylist with audit trail
Auditability: every routing decision for eu_exclusive must emit an audit event with tenant_id, decision, evaluated_rules, fallback taken, timestamp, and operator_id (if overridden)
E2E tests: integration tests that simulate capacity constraints and verify no non-EU egress for hard mode and expected behavior for soft mode
Performance: PDP evaluation should add < 1ms median latency to hot path in 99th percentile for p50/p95/p99 in benchmark harness
Canary: feature can be toggled per-cluster; canary run in eu-west-1 serving 0.5% of production routes before global rollout
tasks: Design policy expression and update PDP grammar (research policy operators and precedence)
Add tenant metadata fields and migration script to save current residency preferences
Implement safelist/denylist datastore (append-only audit log) and operator API
Wire PDP to routing router to enforce hard/soft decisions and expose decision reason codes
Instrument audit events and forward to compliance cluster (kinesis -> s3 vault) and Console
Implement Console UI elements for safelist management and decision logs
Write integration and chaos tests that simulate region capacity loss and forced fallbacks
Prepare runbook for override (operator emergency passthrough) with RBAC controls and KMS-wrapped approvals
decisions: Default behaviour: fail-closed for tenants with eu_holdout=hard (no non-EU egress) to meet strict compliance requirements
Soft mode: logs + alerts but blocks by default; provides a 'review' workflow in Console
Safelist entries require a justification field and an operator signature; stored in append-only store for audit
Emergency override uses a time-limited token (TTL 15m) and must be tied to operator identity; override events are recorded and locked in audit
We will not replicate the entire routing table per region; instead PDP will return a routing label that Router uses to select EU-only tags (less replication, fewer code changes)
Initial implementation will target API router and hosted runtime; Dedicated and Private support will follow via the same PDP contract
testing_plan: Unit tests for PDP predicate 'eu_exclusive' and tenant metadata parsing
Integration tests: simulate a tenant with eu_holdout=hard and force router to choose non-EU model; expect blocked decision and audit event
Load test: run PDP at 10k req/s to measure added latency and ensure p99 < 1.2ms above baseline
Canary: deploy to eu-west-1 with 0.5% traffic; collect audit events and manual compliance signoff
Compliance test: generate example audit report (last 30 days) and validate format against legal team's checklist
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): feature flag behind 'eu_holdout' flag; unit + integration tests merged
Phase 2 (canary): enable in eu-west-1 for 0.5% of traffic; monitor audit logs, PDP latency, error rates
Phase 3 (region expand): if canary stable for 72h and compliance signoff, expand to all EU clusters
Phase 4 (tenant opt-in): Migrate selected pilot tenants to eu_holdout=soft then to hard after validation
Phase 5 (global enforcement): flip default enforcement for newly onboarded regulated tenants; update docs and runbook
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Khan: Created ticket after legal asked for deterministic enforcement; initial spec attached to Confluence link.

2025-02-18 Luca Moretti: Spike completed. PDP grammar change is minimal: added 'eu_exclusive' boolean expression and a decision reason enum. Measurement: added ~0.6ms median latency in local microbenchmarks.
2025-02-21 Maria Gonzalez (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria. Asked to include 'operator_id' in audit event and a console 'review' queue for soft mode; updated spec accordingly.
2025-02-25 SRE: Raised concern about cascade failure when EU capacity is saturated. Suggested a 'circuit breaker' metric for capacity and an alert threshold; plan to add capacity gating rule.
2025-03-01 Security review: initial review OK, but require HSM-backed token for emergency override and retention policy for audit logs (7 years).

2025-03-04 Luca Moretti: Implemented PDP changes and safelist datastore schema. Open PR: route-engine#1582. Began wiring audit events to kinesis; unit tests passing locally. Next: Console UI and canary preparation.
risk: If we block non-EU egress too aggressively without a reliable override and sufficient capacity telemetry, customers may experience silent failures. There's also a risk of increased PDP latency affecting high-throughput endpoints.
mitigation: Implement time-limited emergency override with operator identity and a locked audit trail
Expose clear error surface to SDKs with reason codes and remediation hints
Add PDP performance budget and optimize hot path (caching tenant metadata, precomputed routing labels)
Runchaos tests simulating regional capacity loss and validate observable alerts and runbook steps
